headline: Keep the email check with the handoff
subtext: Email Validation lets recipients and staff save a report of what was checked so the next authorized reviewer has the same context.
image_alt_text: Social graphic titled “Keep the email check with the handoff.” A light-mode Hush Line Tools screenshot shows Raw Email Headers, Validate Headers, Download Report, and a Validation Summary stating that the email appears to originate from the stated sender. Supporting text explains that recipients and staff can save what was checked for the next authorized reviewer.

social.linkedin:
When one staff member hands an email review to another, the next person needs more than a yes or no.

A useful whistleblowing practice is to leave enough context for the next reviewer to understand what was checked. In Hush Line, recipients and staff can paste Raw Email Headers into Email Validation, read the Validation Summary, and Download Report.

That report can support a newsroom, law office, school, or community group during an internal handoff, without asking the next person to reconstruct the check from memory. It follows a plain ISO 37002 principle: handle reports properly and without avoidable delay.

Before the next email handoff, decide where authorized staff will store the downloaded report and who needs to read it.

rationale: The shortlist required a cooldown fallback. Email Validation was selected because it has fewer cooldown violations than Advanced settings and supports a fresh recipient workflow angle. Earlier posts covered authenticity, claim verification, readable summaries, and running the header check; this post instead focuses on preserving review context across an authorized staff handoff. The copy ties that concrete task to proper, timely handling under ISO 37002 and avoids treating a valid result as proof that the email’s claims are true.
copy_brief: Write for recipients and staff using Hush Line day to day, not for platform admins.
